Click‑by‑click handbook

How to actually use IELTS Hub

From the invitation link your centre sends you to reading exactly why an answer was marked wrong. One golden path, in the order you'd really meet it, with the exact button circled on the exact screen you'll see.

  1. 1

    Accept your invitation

    Open the link your centre sends you — it already knows which number you were invited on. Type your full number in to prove it's yours, and press Send code.

  2. 2

    Enter the code

    A one-time code arrives by SMS. Type it into Six-digit code — no password to remember, no account to set up in advance.

  3. 3

    Tell us who you are — the first time only

    The very first time, it also asks for your name and date of birth. Asked once, never shown again: it's what decides which parts of the app treat you as under 18. Press Join.

  4. 4

    This is your home screen

    Your latest and best band, how many mocks you've sat, and everything your centre has assigned you — all in one place, every time you sign in.

  5. 5

    Sit a mock

    Press Sit this mock on anything marked EXAM. The clock starts the moment you're in, and — unlike practice — the audio on a listening mock plays only once, exactly like the real test.

  6. 6

    Answer the questions

    Click an option, type into a gap — whatever the question needs. Nothing here is lost to a bad connection: every answer saves as you go, well before you press Finish.

  7. 7

    Finish when you're done

    Finish asks you to confirm before anything is submitted, so a stray click can't end your mock by accident.

  8. 8

    See your result

    Your band and raw score appear the moment marking finishes — not after a delay, not in a batch overnight.

  9. 9

    See what you got wrong

    Press See what you got wrong underneath your result.

  10. 10

    Read exactly why

    Every question, what you actually wrote, what was accepted — even when you got it right, so you can see the other answers that would also have scored — and a hint on how close a wrong answer was.

  11. 11

    Make it easier to read

    Settings sits in the same corner on every screen, not just the exam itself — home, your result, your review, all of it.

  12. 12

    Pick a text size and a colour

    Three text sizes and four colour combinations, including yellow on black. This is deliberately the same choice the real computer-delivered test offers — a student who needs Extra Large under pressure should already know exactly where to find it.

  13. 13

    It follows you everywhere

    Once set, your choice applies on every screen from then on — not just the one you happened to set it on, and not just for the rest of today.

That's the whole path — sitting a mock, reading your result, and understanding your marking. Everything else in the app (switching numbers, an audio mock's controls) works the same way: a clear button, and a result you can see immediately.
